channel.title: The GW Hatchet - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The GW Hatchet (gwhatchet.com)

item.title: Staff editorial: Part-time faculty pay must be a long-term budget priority
item.description: It's not a good look for the tuition-paying student body to feel that the University isn't allocating enough money to the people who shape their educational experience — the key reason we attend GW.

item.title: Column: GW selling the Virginia campus to Amazon undermines its sustainability commitments
item.description: GW is an institution whose students, faculty and staff care and depend on a just and sustainable future, and the University cannot hypocritically abandon these goals to gain financially from 21st-century robber barons.

item.title: Op-ed: GW’s administration is not complicit in the rise of campus antisemitism
item.description: Speaking up about antisemitism is essential to ensuring that future Jewish students feel safe on campus. But we strongly disagree with claims that the GW administration is complicit in the rise of antisemitism at the school.

item.title: Democratic congressman denounces Iran war, saying it jeopardizes US alliances
item.description: Rep. Don Beyer (D-Va.) said the United States’ involvement in the war in Iran is illegal and immoral, warning that the conflict has strained relationships with key European and Middle Eastern allies.

item.title: 84 percent of GW graduate students ineligible for higher loan limits under Education Department proposal: Goff
item.description: Vice President and Dean of Enrollment Management and Student Success Jay Goff wrote earlier this month that programs including nursing and public health should qualify.

item.title: Board of Trustees taps Vice Chair Mark Chichester as next chair
item.description: GW announced Saturday that the Board of Trustees elected Vice Chair Mark Chichester as its next chair, succeeding longtime leader Grace Speights as the University navigates strategic planning and financial strains.

item.title: GW lifts 10-month freeze on student organization applications
item.description: Officials lifted their yearlong pause on forming new student organizations early, a University spokesperson confirmed, after months of research comparing GW's new organization application and approval process to the University's peer institutions.

item.title: Virginia campus faculty, staff full of questions after GW sidestepped community input on sale
item.description: Faculty and staff operating out of the Virginia Science and Technology Campus said they felt disappointed that officials did not consult them before deciding to sell the campus to Amazon Data Services, though they wish officials’ will engage them in future decision-making.

item.title: Beloved economics professor, principled faculty senator dies at 76
item.description: Colleagues, students and family remember Cordes as a generous, enthusiastic leader who eagerly shared his knowledge of economics with everyone he met.

item.title: Fourth quarter comeback sends women’s basketball to WNIT Super 16
item.description: Women's basketball used a strong fourth quarter to defeat USI and advance to the WNIT's Super 16 on Monday.
